supporting_observations.claim: At 13:53:33 UTC, FILE-RB-01 made a proxy CONNECT request to www.bing.com with user '-' and user agent Go-http-client/1.1. This record does not identify dev.sharma, an RDP session, or the initiating process.
At 14:14:50 UTC, FILE-RB-01 made a proxy CONNECT request to settings-win.data.microsoft.com with user '-' and user agent Microsoft-WNS/10.0. This record likewise provides no RDP-session attribution.
The available FILE-RB-01 proxy records during the collection outage do not establish what occurred in the alerted session and cannot independently support either a malicious or benign disposition.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor-coverage metadata reports that Windows Security, Sysmon, and Zeek connection, DNS, and SSL telemetry were not collected on FILE-RB-01, WS-CPRICE-01, WS-DSHARMA-01, and DC-RB-01 from 13:30 through 14:15 UTC, encompassing the alerted 13:42 session start. This metadata has no record IDs.

No supplied log record directly documents the alerted RDP connection, its source address, authentication, session identifier, or associated commands. The alert description is therefore not independently corroborated by the supplied logs.

Proxy coverage remained available, but the FILE-RB-01 records during the outage identify neither an authenticated user nor an initiating process or RDP session (S21-00300, S21-00470). Missing endpoint and network events cannot be treated as evidence that suspicious activity did not occur.

unrelated_findings: WS-DSHARMA-01 accessed slack.com as dev.sharma at 13:27:43 UTC. Slack is not in the supplied approved-services list; review separately for software/service-policy compliance. This does not establish malicious RDP activity (S21-00081).
